audit.why: 37.5% over 64 games — one of Akshan's worst. The chart gives Vladimir levels 2-3 and everything from first item, and the prose concedes the late game outright. All consistent.
Akshan's Lvl 2-3 window before Sanguine Pool, Vlad's Lvl 6, the first-item stalemate, and his 2+ item AP scaling. Correctly placed; the contents needed the pool-duration correction.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry never states Sanguine Pool's duration or cooldown, so 'don't fire R into the pool' has no timing attached — the reader cannot tell whether that means a moment or a minute. It also garbles Hemoplague, saying he 'amplifies all your incoming damage onto himself nullified', which reads as though the amplification benefits him.
audit.why: Riot's text for Sanguine Pool: 'becoming untargetable for 2 seconds', 350 range, cooldown 28/25/22/19/16. Riot's text for Hemoplague: 'Affected enemies take increased damage for the duration... deals magic damage to infected enemies and heals Vladimir for each enemy Champion hit' — the amplification lands on YOU. The real shape of the matchup is a 100s Comeuppance against a 28s dodge, which is why the pool must be down before you spend the ultimate, and the numbers are what make that legible.
audit.corrected: Sanguine Pool is 2 seconds of untargetability, 350 range, on a 28s rank-1 cooldown. Spend Comeuppance only in its downtime. Hemoplague amplifies the damage you take inside the zone and heals him per champion hit.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Punishing the long W cooldown' with no number, in an entry that identifies that cooldown as Akshan's only opening.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 falling to 16s at rank 5. That is the single largest window in the matchup and naming it turns vague advice into a plan.

audit.whatIsWrong: Grievous Wounds is never mentioned in a matchup entirely defined by his healing.
audit.why: Transfusion heals on a cooldown that drops to 4.6s, and Hemoplague heals him for every champion it hits. Anti-heal is the itemisation lever and the page had none.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tides of Blood being blocked by units is absent.
audit.why: Riot's text: the released blood 'can be blocked by enemy units', so standing behind your own wave denies his area poke entirely. That is free mitigation for a ranged champion.

edits.after: Even with Youmuu's, Vlad pools the instant you lock on — so spend a 100s Comeuppance only once his 28s pool is already down, and take the whole kill window inside that gap.

edits.before: From 6 on, this lane inverts. The second Vlad has R (Hemoplague), every all-in you start gets answered by Sanguine Pool — he W's out of your E swing and your R channel, takes zero while untargetable, then surfaces healed off his Q drain and amplifies all your incoming damage onto himself nullified. Do NOT fire Comeuppance at a Vlad sitting on his pool; your one stored-bullet execute just hits a puddle. Your only profit is poking him out of pool range with Q and punishing the long W cooldown — but his drain sustain plus a developing Rylai's makes even that losing math.
edits.after: From 6 on, this lane inverts. Every all-in you start gets answered by Sanguine Pool — 2 seconds untargetable through your E swing and your R channel, then he surfaces healed off Transfusion. Hemoplague is worse than the entry lets on: the damage amplification lands on YOU, so everything that hits you for the next few seconds hits harder. Do NOT fire Comeuppance at a Vlad with pool available; a 100s ultimate spent into a 28s dodge is the worst trade in the lane. Poke him from outside its 350 range and punish the pool's downtime instead.

edits.before: You lose this outright. A 2+ item full-AP Vlad is the exact scaler your lethality kit cannot kill — he pools your locked-on R, kites your Q with Rylai's slow, and Hemoplague-bursts your shieldless frame in one rotation. Your E-reset snowball never starts because you can't secure the takedown that drops Heroic Swing's cooldown. Convert any early lead into plates and roams with W camouflage before this stretches long; if it hits 25+ minutes you're tower-hugging and team-reliant.

edits.after: Once Sanguine Pool is up, Vlad goes untargetable for 2s on reaction — but it costs him 28s at rank 1, and that gap is your entire trade window.

edits.before: His R Hemoplague plus pool flips your all-in entirely — he phases your committed cooldowns and resurfaces healed and amplified.
edits.after: Hemoplague plus pool flips your all-in — he phases your cooldowns, resurfaces healed, and the zone amplifies the damage you take in it.

notes: The most useful thing this page was missing is the arithmetic: a 100s Comeuppance against a 2-second, 28s-cooldown Sanguine Pool. The entry said 'don't fire into the pool' without ever giving either number, so the reader had no way to plan the window. Also fixed Hemoplague, which the page described as amplifying damage onto Vladimir — it amplifies the damage taken by enemies inside it, i.e. you. Added the 28s pool cooldown, the Grievous Wounds requirement, and the fact that minions block Tides of Blood. The packet's two suspectName flags were both FALSE POSITIVES: 'Sanguine Pools' was the correct name used as a verb, and 'Heroic Swing's' was the correct name with a possessive.
